'''Revaz Valerianovic Gamkrelidze''' ({{lang-ka|რევაზ ვალერიანის ძე გამყრელიძე}}, [[ISO 9984]]: ''Revaz Valeris je Gamqrelije''; February 4, 1927 – May 5, 2025) was a Soviet and Georgian mathematician known for his work in [[optimal control theory]] and related fields. He was a member of the Georgian Academy of Sciences<ref>[http://www.science.org.ge/members/academ-e.html A list of members of the Georgian Academy is available at]</ref> and of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>[http://www.ras.ru/win/db/show_per.asp?P=.id-226.ln-en The page of the Russian Academy of Sciences listing Revaz Gamkrelidze as its member]</ref>

==Background==
After secondary school, Gamkrelidze attended [[Tbilisi State University]].<ref name=Kharat>''Guram Kharatishvili, Memoirs on Differential Equations and Mathematical Physics, "Revaz Gamkrelidze is 70", Razmadze Mathematical Institute, 19973-7,11'' [http://www.jeomj.rmi.acnet.ge/memoirs/vol11/gamkr70.ps.gz]</ref> In his sophomore year, he went to Moscow to study at the mechanics and mathematics faculty of [[Moscow State University]] where he became a student of [[Pontryagin]].<ref name=Kharat />

Gamkrelidze died on May 5, 2025, at the age of 98.<ref>[http://www.viniti.ru/news/483-gamkrelidze-nekrolog Реваз Валерианович Гамкрелидзе] {{in lang|ru}}</ref> He was the brother of the linguist [[Tamaz Gamkrelidze]].

==Work==
At Moscow State University, he initially worked in the fields of algebraic geometry and topology, and derived what is now known as [[Gamkrelidze's formula]].<ref name=Gamkrelidze0>''Computation of Chern cycles of Algebraic Manifolds. (Russian). Dokl. Nauk. SSSR 90(1953), No.4 719–722''</ref> In 1954 he began his work on optimal control. He wrote ''Mathematical Theory of Optimal Processes'' with Pontryagin, [[Vladimir Boltyansky|Boltyanskii]] and [[Evgeniĭ Frolovich Mishchenko|Mishchenko]]. This work was awarded the State Lenin Prize for Science and Technology in 1962.<ref>[[Pontryagin]], [[Vladimir Boltyansky|Boltyanskii]], Gamkrelidze, [[Evgeniĭ Frolovich Mishchenko|Mishchenko]], ''The Mathematical Theory of Optimal Processes, Authorized translation from the Russian'', translated by [[K.N. Trirogoff]], Interscience Publishers, 1962</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.science.org.ge/members/Eng5/Revaz%20Gamkrelidze%20E.pdf |title=Revaz Gamkrelidze's CV at the Georgian Academy of Sciences website |access-date=2011-08-11 |archive-date=2012-03-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120317080208/http://www.science.org.ge/members/Eng5/Revaz%20Gamkrelidze%20E.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> Gamkrelidze was the founding editor of ''[[Encyclopedia of Mathematical Sciences]]''.<ref>See the [https://www.springer.com/series/855 encyclopaedia's website]</ref>
